messages.subject: Model samples on windows and mac, but not linux
parts:
Hello,

I have a model that compiles and samples on Windows (via rstan) on OSX (via rstan or cmdstan), but it only compiles and does not sampl on RedHat linux.

Note that I do not have that problem with other models on linux!


I am getting following message when compiling the model on linux with cmdstan:

--- Linking C++ model ---

icc -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -I src -I stan_2.9.0/src -isystem stan_2.9.0/lib/stan_math_2.9.0/ -isystem stan_2.9.0/lib/stan_math_2.9.0/lib/eigen_3.2.4 -isystem stan_2.9.0/lib/stan_math_2.9.0/lib/boost_1.58.0 -Wall -pipe -DEIGEN_NO_DEBUG -I /cluster/software/VERSIONS/intel-2015.3/mkl//include -DEIGEN_USE_MKL_ALL  -O2 -xAVX -mavx -lpthread  -O3 -o /usit/abel/u1/guidopb/programming/R/representativeness/stan_hlms/stanmodels/ZANB_AE_Reg/ZANB_AE_Reg src/cmdstan/main.cpp -include /usit/abel/u1/guidopb/programming/R/representativeness/stan_hlms/stanmodels/ZANB_AE_Reg/ZANB_AE_Reg.hpp  -L/cluster/software/VERSIONS/intel-2015.3/mkl//lib/intel64 -lmkl_intel_lp64 -lmkl_core -lmkl_sequential -lpthread -lm

In file included from src/cmdstan/command.hpp(94),

                 from src/cmdstan/main.cpp(1):

stan_2.9.0/src/stan/optimization/bfgs.hpp(115): warning #858: type qualifier on return type is meaningless

        const size_t iter_num() const { return _itNum; }

        ^


Following warning/error message repeats when I try to run the model:


Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:

Exception thrown at line 49: std::bad_alloc [origin: bad_alloc]

If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,

but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.


Rejecting initial value:

  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value.



it seems that the following code snippet is causing the problem:



increment_log_prob(bernoulli_logit_log(0,thetas[nzstart:N])

                                + neg_binomial_2_log_log(sy[nzstart:N],

                                                                           etas[nzstart:N],

                                                                           phi));



Does anybody have an idea what could cause this problem?



Best - Guido




########### complete  model code ############

data {

  int<lower=1> N;                // number of data points

  int<lower=0> y[N];             // observations !!sorted from small to large values!!

  int<lower=1> K;                // number parameters

  matrix[N,K] x;                 // individual predictors

}


transformed data {

  // matrices for scaling //

  matrix[N,K] sx;

  int sy[N];

  int idxs[N];

  int nzstart;


  idxs <- sort_indices_asc(y);

  sy <- y[idxs];

  sx <- x[idxs,];  

  

  for (m in 1:num_elements(sy)) {

    if (nzstart == 0) {

      if (sy[m] > 0) nzstart <- m;

    }

  }

}


parameters {

  vector[K] alpha;  // zero inflation coefficients

  vector[K] beta;   // regression coefficients

  // overdispersion of negative binomial

  real<lower=0,upper=pi()/2> phi_unif;

}


transformed parameters {

  real phi;

  phi <- 3*tan(phi_unif);

}


model {

  vector[N] thetas;

  vector[N] etas;


  alpha ~ normal(0,2); # orig scale = 5

  beta ~ normal(0,2); # orig scale = 5


  thetas <- to_vector(sx * to_matrix(alpha));

  etas <- to_vector(sx * to_matrix(beta));


  

  increment_log_prob(bernoulli_logit_log(0,thetas[nzstart:N])

                     + neg_binomial_2_log_log(sy[nzstart:N],

                                              etas[nzstart:N],

                                              phi));

  

  for (k in 1:(nzstart-1)) {increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(log_inv_logit(thetas[k]), 

                                                          log1m_inv_logit(thetas[k]) 

                                                          + neg_binomial_2_log_log(0,etas[k],phi)));}

}

parts:
I found the problem, which was an error of mine in the model code that somehow was tolerated on windows and mac, but not on linux.

the transformed parameters block had these lines

for (m in 1:num_elements(sy)) {
    if (nzstart == 0) {
      if (sy[m] > 0) nzstart <- m;
    }
  }

and the problem was that I had not set the variable nzstart to zero before the loop. 
therefore nzstart got never overwritten and kept as value a very low negative number.
in the model section of the code nzstart with a negative number was used as and index when accessing parts of a matrix.
this can of course not work.

would have been ease to catch that problem if it hadn't worked in the first place under windows,
but the fact that it did let me suspect that the problem ist not with the model code.

hope I didn't take to much of your time!

Guido

parts:
On Saturday, February 27, 2016 at 3:28:45 PM UTC-5, Guido Biele wrote:
I found the problem, which was an error of mine in the model code that somehow was tolerated on windows and mac, but not on linux.

This was been partially fixed a week ago on GitHub. Now integers declared in transformed data are initialized to the most negative integer the computer can handle, whereas in Stan < 2.10 they were initialized to NaN, which is undefined behavior.

Ben
